To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the difference curve between two Weibull distributions almost exactly fitted the left ventricular ( LV ) isovolumic contraction pressure-time curve in all 345 cardiac cycles (3 cycles at each of 3 volumes in 23 dogs), and that the first derivative of that curve also closely fitted that of the pressure-time curve.
the difference curve between two Weibull functions closely fits the LV isov volumic P( t), the first derivative of which also closely fits the LV pressure rise rate ( d P/ dt) curve.

the difference curve between two Weibull functions almost perfectly fits the isovolumic left ventricular pressure-time curve, which suggests the possibility that the left ventricular pressure generation may be characterized by the cumulative breakdown of two counteracting systems, and that the first breakdown system may be related to the generation of the pressure rise phase and the second to the generation of pressure fall phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Weibull distribution function of the LV isov volumic contraction.
a new integrative analysis of the Weibull distribution for cardiac contraction.
the Weibull distribution function as a mathematical model for the cardiac contraction process.

the LV contraction process is a cumulative breakdown process that can be characterized by a Weibull distribution function.
Weibull distribution function is a good model for the LV contraction, and the Weibull distribution model of the heart is a good model of the heart as an integrative system.
the LV isometric pressure generation can be characterized by two Weibull functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Weibull distribution function is a useful tool for analyzing the complex behavior of the heart.
the Weibull function may be useful for describing the integrative behavior of complex systems, such as the heart, and for developing a new systems engineering view of integrative physiology.
the LV contraction is an integrative process, and the Weibull function is a useful mathematical tool to characterize it.

the Weibull distribution function is a good candidate to model cardiac contraction, as well as other physiological processes.
the heart can be modeled as a complex system, and the Weibull distribution function is a powerful tool to characterize the performance of the heart as a complex system.
